decisions.reason: As a burner component tied to the existing radiant-heater business, it likely costs little to keep on offer and still preserves learning value while the firm tests demand.
Because it is presented as a flagship and fits the firm's push toward lower-carbon, electric climate solutions, management would likely keep investing in it while uncertainty resolves.

This halogen infrared heater appears less central to the firm's stated direction and may overlap with stronger electric infrared options, so a growing but disciplined firm would be relatively quick to prune it if traction is limited.
An industrial electric infrared hall heater matches the firm's core customer base and electrification trend, so the option value of keeping it on the market remains high.

The hydrogen-capable dark infrared heater is explicitly strategic, already in real operation, and closely aligned with the firm's future-oriented low-carbon positioning, making withdrawal unlikely in the next year.
